title: Salma and the Greeting of Peace
summary: Salma learns to give the greeting, ask permission, and kiss the hand of elders. (Muslim, on spreading the greeting; QS. An-Nur: 27)
moral: Give the greeting, ask permission before entering, honour elders by kissing their hand, and say thank you.
pages: On the way home from school, Salma visited her grandmother's house. She missed her so much that she ran fast to the door, without saying anything.
Grandma was sitting on the porch and smiled to see her grandchild. 'My dear grandchild, something was forgotten. When we arrive at someone's house, we give the greeting first.' Salma blushed.

Salma repeated politely, 'Assalamu'alaikum, Grandma.' Grandma answered joyfully, 'Wa'alaikumussalam warahmatullahi wabarakatuh.' The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم said, 'Spread the greeting among you, and you will love one another.' (Muslim)
Salma then gently kissed Grandma's hand, a sign of respect for elders. Grandma stroked Salma's head and prayed for her, 'May Allah make you a righteous child.'
Inside the house, Salma saw Grandma's cakes on the table. She wanted to take one at once, but she asked first, 'Grandma, may Salma take a cake?' Grandma nodded happily, 'Yes, take one, dear.'

Salma took the cake with her right hand and said, 'Jazakillah khairan, Grandma.' They sat together enjoying the cakes. Salma learned: give the greeting, ask permission, kiss the hand of elders, and say thank you. The end.
